analysis.title: Inflation Update: October 2026 CPI Preview
key_insights: MUFG forecasts October 2026 headline CPI at 0.29% MoM and core CPI at 0.23% MoM, in line with the median Bloomberg contributor estimate.
MUFG sees risks tilted to a stronger core CPI. Monthly core readings below 0.15% have been uncommon since 2022, and more items would need significant disinflation for core to come in below 0.2% MoM.

A reversal in owners' equivalent rent (OER) after last month's unusual strength could soften the print. Elevated shipping costs and reinstituted tariffs may accelerate core goods contributions and offset part of that improvement.
Airline fares, lodging and recreational services prices are expected to push October core CPI higher.

MUFG's base case is a muted market reaction to a 0.2% MoM core print. Markets are focused on the benefits of lower oil prices and may treat October CPI as old news. Fed funds futures still price a December hike.
A very strong October NFP was needed to partially stop last week's flight-to-safety Treasury rally, so the bar is also high for CPI to trigger a rates selloff.
Last month's stronger than expected core CPI did not trigger a lasting selloff. MUFG expects equity market fragility to keep dominating the narrative.
A 0.1% MoM core reading would move December hike odds closer to MUFG's 55-60% expectation.

tension_points.bull_case: A strong OER reversal after last month's unusual strength could produce a softer print, and a 0.1% MoM core reading would ease December hike odds toward MUFG's 55-60%.
tension_points.bear_case: Elevated shipping costs and reinstituted tariffs lift core goods, and airline fares, lodging and recreational services add upward pressure, tilting risks to a stronger core print.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A core CPI reading below 0.2% MoM would need significant disinflation across more items, which MUFG considers unlikely.
